source: Public third-party ActionShift frozen PPO unchanged, published HF revision 6bdeb28810330ab5425ccd629bb561c58a56ff85
probe: One native zero-6D arm delta on the known accumulated-target Panda controller, gripper command retained from previous frozen policy step. The PPO does not act during the probe step for any arm. Any reset/current achieved EE pose and probe response are used, but target_pose field in observation is discarded and controller target getter NEVER called for classifier before episode end.

classifier.observed_feature: achieved end-effector XYZ AFTER common zero-native-delta probe
classifier.candidate_targets: complete previous history plus both candidate histories after ACK uncertainty, generated by separately implemented published action-only history target observer
classifier.score: euclidean distance in meters from observed achieved XYZ to each candidate commanded-target XYZ
classifier.condition: If best-second distance margin <2mm OR target hypotheses have <=2mm separation, abstain and stop before next PPO action. Otherwise select nearest target history without privileged goal read.
classifier.rotation: ignored by binary classifier; rotation difference, when present, only audited; cannot claim general 6DoF observability

access.source_action_chart: known Panda achieved-relative to target-relative mapping

measure: zero vs privileged read task successes
controller state audit AFTER outcome only
limitations: Nearest-target is heuristic and uses controller frame/model but no runtime commanded target getter
unmodeled servo lag/contact and rotations can make nearest-target erroneous
one extra native physics step is a real intervention and has task performance cost
same Panda single simulator controller family, no hardware, no ROS/TCP loss
candidate goals can overlap or be indistinguishable; must abstain
the full action trajectory is not equal to source policy trajectory
success_criterion: This is a genuinely falsifiable negative-prone mechanism test. Positive result requires reduced blind-error with reasonable coverage AND improved paired task success over equally-probed optimistic/pessimistic, not simply one successful trajectory.
